```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Park_2023_pregabalin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Park_2023_pregabalin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.12793/tcp.2023.31.e20> (open access, PMC10772055)

# Population

Park 2023 studied YHD1119, a once-daily sustained-release pregabalin tablet, in
16 Korean adults (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05012436) grouped by screening MDRD
eGFR. Cohort A (near-normal renal function, eGFR > 60 mL/min/1.73 m^2, n = 8,
all male, median age 38 years, median weight 70.6 kg, median eGFR 91.5
[79.0-117.0]) received a single 75 mg tablet (Period 1) and, after a four-day
washout, a single 150 mg tablet (Period 2). Cohort B (moderate renal
impairment, eGFR 30-60 mL/min/1.73 m^2, n = 8, 7 male, median age 60 years,
median weight 73.5 kg, median eGFR 45.5 [36.0-59.0]) received a single 75 mg
tablet only. Doses were taken 30 minutes after a standard meal, and plasma was
sampled pre-dose and 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 24, 48 and 72 h
post-dose (Methods; demographics in Table 1).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Park_2023_pregabalin")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| One-compartment, first-order absorption with lag, first-order elimination | n/a | Methods 'Population PK analysis'; Results 'Population PK analysis' |
| `CL/F = CL_pop * min(eGFR, BP) / 73` | n/a | Results 'Population PK analysis' (linear in eGFR, centred, up to the breakpoint); centring value back-solved from Figure 4 (see below) |
| `ltlag` | log(0.889 h) | Table 4 'Tlag, h' |
| `lka` | log(0.347 1/h) | Table 4 'ka, h-1' |
| `lvc` | log(61.7 L) | Table 4 'Vd/F, L' |
| `lcl` | log(5.55 L/h) | Table 4 'CL/F, L/h' |
| `lcrcl_hinge` | log(91.2 mL/min/1.73 m^2) | Table 4 'Breakpoint' |
| `etalcl` | 0.242^2 = 0.0586 | Table 4 BSV 'CL/F, CV (%)' = 0.242 (24.6%) |
| `etalvc` | 0.147^2 = 0.0216 | Table 4 BSV 'Vd/F, CV (%)' = 0.147 (14.8%) |
| `etaiov_tlag_1`, `etaiov_tlag_2` | 0.726^2 = 0.527 | Table 4 IOV 'Tlag, CV (%)' = 0.726 (83.3%) |
| `propSd` | 0.286 | Table 4 'Proportional error' |

Monolix reports the random-effect standard deviation omega; the CV in
parentheses in Table 4 is `sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)` (for example
`sqrt(exp(0.242^2) - 1) = 0.246`), which confirms the scale. The nlmixr2
variances are therefore `omega^2`.

# Centring value of eGFR

The paper states that eGFR enters CL/F "in a linear relationship centered on
the weighted mean of eGFR up to the breakpoint" but does not print that
weighted mean. Because CL/F is proportional to eGFR, the centring value sets
the absolute clearance of every subject, so it cannot be left at an arbitrary
round number. The maintainers digitised the three median curves of Figure 4
(steady state after once-daily dosing at eGFR 90 and 45 mL/min/1.73 m^2) from
the published image and found the centring value that reproduces them. A
stochastic re-simulation of the median curves implied 72.3, 73.7 and 73.5 for
the three curves, and a typical-value calculation from the curve AUCs gave
73.1-75.0, so the model uses 73 mL/min/1.73 m^2. As a cross-check, the mean of
the two cohort median eGFRs weighted by the number of occasions per cohort
(two in Cohort A, capped at the breakpoint, one in Cohort B) is
`(2 * 91.2 + 45.5) / 3 = 76.0`.

```{r fig4-digitised}
# Median steady-state concentrations (ng/mL) read from Figure 4 of Park 2023.
# t = 0 is the pre-dose trough of the steady-state interval.
fig4_digitised <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~`75 mg, eGFR 90`, ~`150 mg, eGFR 90`, ~`75 mg, eGFR 45`,
  0,  154,  317,  561,
  2,  473,  953,  828,
  4,  732, 1469, 1131,
  6,  783, 1563, 1226,
  8,  729, 1475, 1206,
  10, 638, 1289, 1144,
  12, 534, 1088, 1055,
  14, 446,  899,  960,
  16, 363,  740,  868,
  18, 295,  607,  783,
  20, 238,  491,  701,
  22, 191,  396,  628,
  24, 156,  322,  563
) |>
  pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "scenario", values_to = "Cc")
```

# Virtual cohort

Observed data are not available. The virtual cohorts below draw eGFR from
truncated normal distributions centred on each cohort's Table 1 median and
bounded by its range. Cohort A subjects carry both periods (75 mg at time 0 on
occasion 1, 150 mg at 168 h on occasion 2), as in the study's one-sequence
crossover; Cohort B subjects receive 75 mg on occasion 1 only.

```{r cohort}
# set.seed() fixes the covariate draws; rxSetSeed() fixes rxode2's own
# random-effect draws for a given rxode2 build and thread count only, so all
# assertions below are on medians and robust quantiles.
set.seed(20231201)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20231201)

draw_trunc <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  x <- rnorm(n * 4, mean, sd)
  x <- x[x >= lo & x <= hi]
  x[seq_len(n)]
}

n_per_cohort <- 150L
sample_times <- c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 24, 48, 72)
plot_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.25), seq(25, 72, by = 1))))
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(sample_times, plot_times)))

make_period <- function(ids, egfr, dose, occ, t0) {
  dose_rows <- tibble(
    id = ids, time = t0, amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot",
    CRCL = egfr, OCC = occ
  )
  obs_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(
    tibble(id = ids, CRCL = egfr), time = t0 + obs_times
  ) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", OCC = occ)
  bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows)
}

ids_a <- seq_len(n_per_cohort)
ids_b <- n_per_cohort + seq_len(n_per_cohort)
egfr_a <- draw_trunc(n_per_cohort, 91.5, 10, 79, 117)
egfr_b <- draw_trunc(n_per_cohort, 45.5, 7, 36, 59)

events <- bind_rows(
  make_period(ids_a, egfr_a, 75, 1L, 0),
  make_period(ids_a, egfr_a, 150, 2L, 168),
  make_period(ids_b, egfr_b, 75, 1L, 0)
) |>
  mutate(cohort = ifelse(id %in% ids_a, "A", "B")) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Park_2023_pregabalin")
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("cohort", "OCC")) |>
  as.data.frame()

# Split Cohort A into its two periods and put each period on its own
# time-after-dose axis.
sim_tad <- sim |>
  mutate(
    period_start = ifelse(cohort == "A" & OCC == 2, 168, 0),
    tad = time - period_start,
    treatment = case_when(
      cohort == "A" & OCC == 1 ~ "Cohort A, 75 mg",
      cohort == "A" & OCC == 2 ~ "Cohort A, 150 mg",
      TRUE ~ "Cohort B, 75 mg"
    )
  ) |>
  filter(tad >= 0, tad <= 72)
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 1: mean concentration-time profiles

```{r figure-1, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
# Replicates Figure 1 of Park 2023 (mean +/- SD by cohort and period), on
# the paper's sampling times.
sim_tad |>
  filter(tad %in% sample_times) |>
  group_by(treatment, tad) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(Cc), sd = sd(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, mean, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = pmax(mean - sd, 0), ymax = mean + sd), width = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Pregabalin (ng/mL)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 1A of Park 2023 (simulated)."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Figure 3: visual predictive check

```{r figure-3, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5}
# Replicates the simulated percentile bands of Figure 3 of Park 2023
# (10th, 50th and 90th percentiles), including residual error.
sim_tad |>
  filter(tad %in% plot_times) |>
  group_by(treatment, tad) |>
  summarise(
    p10 = quantile(sim, 0.1), p50 = quantile(sim, 0.5),
    p90 = quantile(sim, 0.9), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Pregabalin (ng/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Park 2023: simulated 10th-90th percentiles and median."
  )
```

## Figure 4: steady state at eGFR 90 and 45 mL/min/1.73 m^2

```{r figure-4, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
n_ss <- 200L
ss_scenarios <- tibble(
  scenario = c("75 mg, eGFR 90", "150 mg, eGFR 90", "75 mg, eGFR 45"),
  dose = c(75, 150, 75),
  egfr = c(90, 90, 45)
)
ss_events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(ss_scenarios)), function(i) {
  ids <- (i - 1) * n_ss + seq_len(n_ss)
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = seq(0, 13 * 24, by = 24)) |>
    mutate(amt = ss_scenarios$dose[i], evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = 312 + seq(0, 24, by = 0.5)) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(CRCL = ss_scenarios$egfr[i], OCC = 1L, scenario = ss_scenarios$scenario[i])
})) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ss_events, keep = "scenario") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(tad = time - 312)

ss_summary <- sim_ss |>
  group_by(scenario, tad) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), p50 = median(Cc), p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(ss_summary, aes(tad, colour = scenario, fill = scenario)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  geom_point(data = fig4_digitised, aes(time, Cc), shape = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose at steady state (h)", y = "Pregabalin (ng/mL)",
    colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 4 of Park 2023. Lines: simulated median;",
      "shading: 5th-95th percentile; open circles: median digitised from the paper."
    )
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The simulated median curves reproduce the digitised ones. The median AUC over
the dosing interval differs from the digitised AUC by:

```{r figure-4-check}
auc_trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
fig4_check <- ss_summary |>
  filter(tad %in% fig4_digitised$time) |>
  inner_join(fig4_digitised, by = c("scenario", tad = "time")) |>
  group_by(scenario) |>
  summarise(
    auc_simulated = auc_trap(tad, p50),
    auc_digitised = auc_trap(tad, Cc),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auc_simulated / auc_digitised - 1))

fig4_check |>
  mutate(across(c(auc_simulated, auc_digitised), round), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  rename(
    Scenario = scenario,
    "Simulated median AUC0-24 (ng*h/mL)" = auc_simulated,
    "Digitised AUC0-24 (ng*h/mL)" = auc_digitised,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

# A wrong centring value, clearance or volume moves all three curves together
# by tens of percent; digitisation error is a few percent.
stopifnot(all(abs(fig4_check$pct_diff) < 10))
```

# PKNCA validation

NCA uses the paper's sampling schedule. Concentrations below the 20 ng/mL
lower limit of quantification are dropped after the pre-dose sample, as in the
paper's NCA.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim_tad |>
  filter(tad %in% sample_times, !is.na(Cc)) |>
  filter(tad == 0 | Cc >= 20) |>
  select(id, time = tad, Cc, treatment)

sim_nca <- bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, treatment, time)

dose_df <- sim_tad |>
  distinct(id, treatment) |>
  mutate(time = 0, amt = ifelse(treatment == "Cohort A, 150 mg", 150, 75))

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE,
  half.life = TRUE, cl.obs = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

## Comparison against published NCA

Table 2 of Park 2023 reports arithmetic means (median for Tmax). The simulated
summaries below are aggregated the same way before comparison. Dose is in mg
and concentration in ng/mL, so PKNCA's `cl.obs` is in mg/(ng*h/mL) and is
multiplied by 1000 to give L/h.

```{r nca_compare}
nca_long <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast", "aucinf.obs", "half.life", "cl.obs")) |>
  mutate(PPORRES = ifelse(PPTESTCD == "cl.obs", 1000 * PPORRES, PPORRES))

sim_summary <- nca_long |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(
    value = ifelse(PPTESTCD[1] == "tmax", median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), mean(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = value)

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~auclast, ~aucinf.obs, ~tmax, ~half.life, ~cl.obs,
  "Cohort A, 75 mg", 873.19, 9613.56, 10809.64, 5.0, 6.69, 7.46,
  "Cohort A, 150 mg", 1678.22, 20554.31, 22509.18, 5.0, 7.81, 7.31,
  "Cohort B, 75 mg", 1065.16, 23766.29, 25267.91, 5.5, 13.47, 3.37
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_summary,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(
    cmax = "ng/mL", auclast = "ng*h/mL", aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL",
    tmax = "h", half.life = "h", cl.obs = "L/h"
  ),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Simulated vs. published (Park 2023 Table 2) NCA. * differs from reference by >20%."
)
```

AUC, half-life and CL/F agree with Table 2 to within about 12%. Simulated
Cmax runs 15-20% below the observed means and Tmax is later, most visibly
in Cohort B. This is a property of the published model rather than of the
transcription: the typical-value one-compartment profile with ka = 0.347 1/h
and V/F = 61.7 L peaks near 710 ng/mL after 75 mg at eGFR 91 mL/min/1.73 m^2,
below the observed mean of 873 ng/mL, while the model's own steady-state
simulations in Figure 4 are reproduced within a few percent above. The paper
notes that a structural model other than the one-compartment model "may
produce a better-fitting outcome" and kept it for comparability with earlier
pregabalin models.

```{r nca_ratio}
# Table 3 of Park 2023: geometric mean ratios (Cohort B 75 mg over each
# Cohort A period) for Cmax and AUClast.
gm <- nca_long |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast")) |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(gm = exp(mean(log(PPORRES))), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = treatment, values_from = gm)

gmr <- tibble(
  Comparison = c("Cohort B (75 mg) / Cohort A (75 mg)", "Cohort B (75 mg) / Cohort A (150 mg)"),
  `Cmax simulated` = c(
    gm$`Cohort B, 75 mg`[gm$PPTESTCD == "cmax"] / gm$`Cohort A, 75 mg`[gm$PPTESTCD == "cmax"],
    gm$`Cohort B, 75 mg`[gm$PPTESTCD == "cmax"] / gm$`Cohort A, 150 mg`[gm$PPTESTCD == "cmax"]
  ),
  `Cmax published` = c(1.2273, 0.6476),
  `AUClast simulated` = c(
    gm$`Cohort B, 75 mg`[gm$PPTESTCD == "auclast"] / gm$`Cohort A, 75 mg`[gm$PPTESTCD == "auclast"],
    gm$`Cohort B, 75 mg`[gm$PPTESTCD == "auclast"] / gm$`Cohort A, 150 mg`[gm$PPTESTCD == "auclast"]
  ),
  `AUClast published` = c(2.4146, 1.1471)
)
knitr::kable(gmr, digits = 3, caption = "Geometric mean ratios (Park 2023 Table 3).")
```

The simulated AUClast ratio of Cohort B to Cohort A is close to 2, which is
the ratio the proportional eGFR model implies at the two cohort medians
(`min(91.5, 91.2) / 45.5 = 2.0`). The observed ratio of 2.41 reflects the
eight study subjects of each cohort, whose individual eGFR values and CL/F
deviations are not published.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **eGFR centring value (73 mL/min/1.73 m^2).** Not printed in the paper; the
  maintainers back-solved it from the digitised median curves of Figure 4, as
  described above. The CL/F estimate of 5.55 L/h is therefore the typical
  CL/F at an eGFR of 73 mL/min/1.73 m^2.
- **Breakpoint.** Table 4 gives 91.2 mL/min/1.73 m^2; the Results text says
  the breakpoint "was fixed at the estimated value of 92.10" for the
  bootstrap. The model uses the tabulated final estimate, 91.2; the
  difference changes CL/F by at most 1% and only for eGFR above 91.2.
- **Form of the eGFR effect.** The paper describes a linear relationship
  through the origin (CL/F proportional to eGFR, no separately estimated
  slope in Table 4) capped at the breakpoint; the model encodes
  `CL/F = 5.55 * min(eGFR, 91.2) / 73`.
- **Inter-occasion variability.** IOV on Tlag is encoded with one eta per
  occasion sharing a single variance; pass `OCC = 1` for single-occasion
  simulation. The steady-state simulation of Figure 4 uses one occasion for
  all doses, so its lag time varies between subjects but not between doses.
- **Virtual cohort.** eGFR was drawn from truncated normal distributions
  around each cohort's Table 1 median; individual eGFR values and their time
  course were not published. The study measured eGFR as a time-varying
  covariate, while only the screening values are reported.
- **BQL data.** The model was fitted with the M4 method for samples below the
  20 ng/mL LLOQ. The simulation does not censor; the NCA drops post-dose
  simulated concentrations below 20 ng/mL to mirror the paper's NCA.
- **NCA comparison.** The virtual cohorts are larger than the 8-subject study
  cohorts and their eGFR distribution is an approximation, so differences of
  the order of the published between-subject SDs are expected.
- **Errata.** No correction notice for this article was found in PubMed as of
  2026-10-28.
